text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Ruling Christian Democrats (CDU) say they want to reduce tax rates for all taxpayers and have no plans to change tax rules for pensions.
- Frankfurt book fair opens.
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl urges fellow Germans to tackle the problems of unification with resolve.
- Tens of thousands of Daimler-Benz workers protest at company's plans to cut sick pay.
- A quarter of taxpayers' money is being wasted, lobby group says.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- DGB trade union federation calls on employers to abandon "policy of confrontation" on sick pay.
- CDU proposes new tax on some forms of investment.
- Works councils demand a decision on fate of Eurofighter project.
- Biotechnology sector could create up to 100,000 jobs by the year 2000 if Germany seizes opportunities in the sector, new research says.
- Koblenz court bans advertising by fax.
HANDELSBLATT
- Handelsblatt indicator on future growth indicates healthy picture for west German economy.
- Analysts estimate shares in Deutsche Telekom will be offered at between 25 and 30 marks at its floatation later this year.
- Post Minister Wolfgang Boetsch wants to force through increase in postage costs despite opposition of Free Democrat coalition partners.
DIE WELT
- CDU tax plans include new tax on shareholders.
- Kohl says reconstruction in eastern Germany will continue for years to come.
- OeTV white-collar union re-elects Herbert Mai as leader with large majority.
- IWG reserach institute predicts Germany this year will miss both debt and deficit criteria for planned European single currency.
